faqs.a: 20% is the traditional sweet spot: it avoids mortgage insurance in most markets and gets better rates. But many first-time buyers put down 5–10% and pay insurance instead — waiting years to reach 20% while prices rise can cost more than the insurance.
faqs.q: How much down payment do I need for a house?

faqs.a: Mostly, but not absolutely. Beyond 20%, each extra percent saves a little interest but locks cash into an illiquid asset. Keep 3–6 months of expenses liquid no matter what — a house with no emergency fund is a fragile house.
faqs.q: Is a bigger down payment always better?

faqs.a: If you need it within 3 years, keep it safe — high-yield savings or short FDs. Markets can drop 20% right when you need the money. For horizons beyond 5 years, a conservative mix can help you keep up with rising prices.
faqs.q: Should I invest my down payment savings or keep it safe?

faqs.a: Budget an extra 2–5% of the price for stamp duty, registration, legal fees, and moving. In India, stamp duty plus registration alone often runs 5–7%. Your true 'cash needed' is the down payment plus these — plan for both.
Please don't. The month after you buy, something will break — and without reserves you'll reach for credit cards at 36% APR. Save the down payment separately; the emergency fund stays untouched.
faqs.q: Can I use my emergency fund as a down payment?

faqs.a: Directly: every extra rupee down is one less rupee borrowed, plus interest saved over the whole loan. On a 20-year loan at 9%, each ₹1 lakh extra down saves roughly ₹2.16 lakh in total payments.
faqs.q: Does the down payment affect my EMI?

down-payment-calculator.formula:
Down payment = home price x down payment % / 100.
Loan amount = home price - down payment.
Monthly savings = down payment / months to save.
Example: 5,000,000 x 20% = 1,000,000; 1,000,000 / 36 = 27,777.78/month.
howTo: Enter the home price you're targeting.
Set how many months you have to save.
Read the down payment, loan amount, and monthly savings target.
keyFacts: 20% down is the classic target — it usually avoids private mortgage insurance.
A bigger down payment shrinks your loan, your EMI, and your total interest.
But draining every rupee for the down payment leaves no emergency buffer — balance matters.
Most buyers take 2–5 years to save a down payment; automating it is the key.
Don't forget closing costs: add another 2–5% of the price on top.

down-payment-calculator.quickAnswer: On a ₹5,000,000 home with 20% down, you need ₹1,000,000 upfront and will borrow ₹4,000,000. Saving for it over 36 months means setting aside ₹27,778 every month. A bigger down payment also means a smaller loan, less interest, and often no mortgage insurance.
down-payment-calculator.tagline: Plan your home down payment — amount, loan size, and the monthly savings to get there.
down-payment-calculator.workedExample:
Home price ₹5,000,000, 20% down, 36 months to save:
1. Down payment = 5,000,000 x 20 / 100 = ₹1,000,000.
2. Loan amount = 5,000,000 - 1,000,000 = ₹4,000,000.
3. Monthly savings = 1,000,000 / 36 = ₹27,777.78.
4. Set up an automatic transfer of ₹27,778 on payday and the goal funds itself.
